rationale: Plural noun designating an archonic operation; etymology likely on ⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'carry forth' family with reduplication or extension. Cf. accumulated ⲟ̄ⲁⲗⲟ̄ⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'draw out, lift forth' and ⲁⲗⲱⲭϩ̅ 'snatch out.' The morphology -ⲁⲁⲛ- is unclear; possibly a Lyc. action-noun infix. Tentative.

Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'fall, sink' with directional 'upon.' The verb governs the punitive descent of either the archons themselves (collapsing) or external agents (e.g. avenging angels) upon the archons before their imprisonment.
Lycopolitan variant of ⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'manner, fashion'? Or possibly an obscure noun meaning 'kind' or 'order.' Used here in 'the X of [exposition] of all the apocalypses.' Confidence low.

ⲥⲁϣϩ (Lyc. seven, in glossary as ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲁϣϩ 'seventh') + ⲙⲁⲓⲧ 'paths' (= ⲙⲟⲉⲓⲧ). Manichaean cosmographic term for the seven outer cosmic paths into which the dark powers are cast — paralleling the seven firmaments and seven works elsewhere in the Kephalaia.
Lycopolitan plural variant of accumulated ⲛⲍⲟⲩⲍⲉ 'abortions.' ϣⲁⲣⲡⲧ here likely ϣⲣⲡ̄/ϣⲱⲣⲡ̄ derivation; the archonic abortions cast into the great sea is a standard Manichaean cosmogonic motif.
